summary: Global markets are displaying a cautiously mixed mood, with investors navigating a complex backdrop of geopolitical developments and pivotal corporate earnings. On the macro front, Putin's agreement to resume three-way peace talks with Ukraine and the U.S. offered a tentative geopolitical tailwind, while stalled Iran-U.S. diplomacy rattled Gulf markets and kept oil prices elevated, with Saudi crude exports hitting a five-month high in August adding further supply-side complexity. In equity markets, Meta shares advanced ahead of after-the-bell earnings as investors sought clarity on AI monetization and ad revenue trends, Salesforce drew attention for its renewed M&A activity aimed at shoring up slower-growing business lines, and AI infrastructure player Nebius pushed back against skepticism over neoclouds by citing rising AI computing prices. The primary risk factors investors are monitoring include persistent inflation — underscored by the UK's hot CPI print limiting FTSE 100 gains — elevated oil prices pressuring import-dependent emerging markets like India, and ongoing Middle East tensions involving Yemen's Houthis and the unresolved Iran standoff keeping energy markets on edge. In the short term, the market's direction will hinge heavily on Big Tech earnings results, particularly Meta's report, alongside any concrete progress in Ukraine peace negotiations and whether oil supply dynamics shift materially given China's crude stockpile drawdowns and Saudi export volumes.
